newsitem.title: USA: Albright to shun swearing-in of new HK assembly.
newsitem.headline: Albright to shun swearing-in of new HK assembly.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, who will attend the handover of Hong Kong to China on July 1, will not attend the swearing-in of a new China-backed legislature there, the State Department said on Monday.
"She's not yet been invited to any ceremony that would actually swear in the new provisional legislature," said State Department spokeman Nicholas Burns.
"But I can tell you if she were to be invited, she would not attend that ceremony ... because it wouldn't be appropriate," Burns told reporters.

The Washington Post reported on Saturday that China planned to use the all-night June 30-July 1 ceremony to take control of Hong Kong from Britain as a chance to swear in its handpicked legislature before international dignitaries.
This, the newspaper said, was creating a diplomatic dilemma for Albright and other visiting officials opposed to Beijing's setting up the new lawmaking body.

"We have never believed that the appointment of a provisional legislature is justified or necessary," Burns said. "There is a pefectly good legislature in place, it's a democratically elected legislature for the people of Hong Kong, the Legislative Council."
Burns said U.S. Consul-General in Hong Kong Richard Boucher had "made very clear" that Albright would not attend any swearing-in ceremony.
The State Department says Albright is going to Hong Kong to reaffirm support for the territory's democratic system.

The 60 members of the provisional legislature were carefully selected into office under Beijing's auspices in December to replace the existing Legislative Council, which the Hong Kong voters elected in 1995.
At a meeting in China on Saturday, the new shadow legislators passed a string of laws to come into effect after the territory reverts to Chinese rule.
